Specify a four-component stochastic frontier model

Source: R/create_sfmodel4.R
create_sfmodel4_exp.Rd

Sets up the model object that the add_* functions operate on. The two functions differ only in the distribution assumed for the one-sided terms, which determines the class of the object and hence the methods that apply to it.

create_sfmodel4_exp(
  formula,
  data,
  id,
  type = c("production", "cost"),
  iterations = 20000,
  burnin = 2000,
  thin = 1
)

create_sfmodel4_hn(
  formula,
  data,
  id,
  type = c("production", "cost"),
  iterations = 20000,
  burnin = 2000,
  thin = 1
)

Arguments

formula

a model formula describing the frontier.

data

a data frame containing the variables in formula.

id

either the name of a variable in data or a vector of the same length as the data, identifying the units. Required, since the model cannot separate its components without repeated observations.

type

either "production" or "cost".

iterations

number of iterations retained after burn-in, before thinning.

burnin

number of discarded iterations.

thin

thinning interval. iterations must be a multiple of it.

Value

An object of class "sfmodel4_exp" or "sfmodel4_hn", both inheriting from "sfmodel4" and "sfmodel".

Details

The model is $$y_{it} = x_{it}' \beta + \mu_i - \eta_i - u_{it} + v_{it}, \quad v_{it} \sim N(0, \sigma_v^2),$$ for a production frontier, with the signs of \(\eta\) and \(u\) reversed for a cost frontier. Its four components are

\(\mu_i \sim N(0, \sigma_\mu^2)\)

an unrestricted unit effect, which is latent heterogeneity and not inefficiency: technology, market or business model, anything that makes a unit persistently different for reasons unrelated to how well it operates.

\(\eta_i \ge 0\)

persistent inefficiency, constant over a unit's observations.

\(v_{it}\)

symmetric noise.

\(u_{it} \ge 0\)

transient inefficiency, varying within a unit.

As in the two-component models, the response is assumed to be on a logarithmic scale, which is what makes \(\exp(-\eta_i)\) and \(\exp(-u_{it})\) efficiencies rather than quantities in the units of the output. See create_sfmodel_exp.

This is the specification of Kumbhakar, Lien and Hjalmarsson (2014), Colombi et al. (2014) and Tsionas and Kumbhakar (2014). The reason to prefer it over the time-invariant panel model of create_sfmodel_exp is that the latter has no \(\mu_i\), so every persistent difference between units is booked as inefficiency; and no \(u_{it}\), so nothing within a unit can vary. Separating the two matters whenever the question is about movement in efficiency over time rather than about a ranking of units.

The price is identification. \(\mu_i\) and \(\eta_i\) are both unit-specific and are told apart only by the sign restriction on \(\eta\) and by the distributional assumptions, while the mean of \(\eta\) is in addition hard to separate from the intercept of the frontier.

What the data determine sharply is the combination \(\mu_i - \eta_i\). How that combination is divided between the two depends on which of them has the wider spread: where the unit effect dominates, it is recovered well and the persistent inefficiency term is not, and where it is small the reverse holds. The transient term is unaffected, since it is identified within a unit. This is a property of the model rather than of the sampler, and it is worth a prior sensitivity check before reading much into the split. The combination itself, and therefore the fitted frontier, is reliable either way.

Both one-sided terms follow the same family, half-normal or exponential, with separate parameters.

References

Colombi, R., Kumbhakar, S. C., Martini, G., & Vittadini, G. (2014). Closed-skew normality in stochastic frontiers with individual effects and long/short-run efficiency. Journal of Productivity Analysis, 42(2), 123–136.

Kumbhakar, S. C., Lien, G., & Hjalmarsson, L. (2014). Technical efficiency in competing panel data models: A study of Norwegian grain farming. Journal of Productivity Analysis, 41(2), 321–337.

Tsionas, E. G., & Kumbhakar, S. C. (2014). Firm heterogeneity, persistent and transient technical inefficiency: A generalized true random-effects model. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 29(1), 110–132.

See also

create_sfmodel_exp for the two-component models, add_priors, efficiency, sim_sf4

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf4(n = 60, n_time = 8, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3))

model <- create_sfmodel4_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, id = "id",
                             iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model
#> Four-component Bayesian stochastic frontier model
#> 
#> Frontier:           production
#> Inefficiency:       exponential, persistent and transient
#> Observations:       480
#> Coefficients:       3
#> Inefficiency terms: 60 (one per unit, time invariant)
#> Iterations:         500 after 200 burn-in, thinning 1
#> 
#> Specification:
#>   priors         not set
#>   initial values not set
#>   seed           not set
#>   posterior      not simulated
